column1: # Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave (Switch 2, v131072). Plays on the Mac: see README.md

# Intelligent Systems' engine on NintendoWare (G3d / Ui2d / Vfx / Atk), PhysX 5.6, SDK 22.2.0, NVN2 (Ampere shaders); modules main + subsdk2 (movie) + sdk. subsdk0 (DLSS) and subsdk1 (CUDA) are not loaded: main imports nothing from them.
# Packed from a dump folder with scripts/pack_dump.py. Shaders: Shaders/*.bfsha.zst (zstd of FSHA).
# ---- Identity ----
title_id
program_id
name
ipa
app_category
pad_layout
# ---- Versions ----
build
package
shader_versions
# ---- Frame rate ----
# The game's graphics object holds its target frame rate (60 for the title and menus, 30 for gameplay) and steps the game by 60 / target. The rewriter finds the field by its
# readers in any build (dm/tools/fps_target.py), the host writes the target there (hle_fpslock.c), and the game asks for the matching present interval itself.
# Android: 30, the rate the game itself plays at, menus included (a phone holds it with room; the in-game panel's Frame rate cap picks 60). The Mac's note runs it at 60 and
# 120 (fps_max, not on Android): README.md, Frame rate
fps_target
# ---- Graphics ----
# The game sets the near=0 NVN depth mode (nvnDeviceSetDepthMode): offline pipeline bases take the main0_z vertex entries. Without the key the bundled archive was made for
# near=-w, the host refused it ("the game's depth mode is not the one built for") and every Mac built its own 872 MB of bases on first start
depth_mode
# Android, Qualcomm's stock driver (Adreno 830, 512.800.77): the light grid's compute shader lost the device at its first dispatch, at the title (vkQueueSubmit -4);
# its subgroup operations run as one invocation on Qualcomm's own driver (a workaround: dm/games/README.md subgroup_one_lane)
subgroup_one_lane
# Android: the game's DLSS (NVN2) runs on vka's stand-in, Snapdragon GSR2 3-pass (vka_dlss.c); the launcher's Upscaler row offers its modes, with Motion clarity
# (DM_VK_GSR2_CLARITY) and Temporal sharpness (DM_VK_DLSS_SHARP) sliders, in Game settings and the in-game panel
dlss_standin
# Android: the 2560x1440 AV1 movies (50-70 Mbit/s) decode on dav1d frame-parallel, not the phone's hardware decoder: Qualcomm's c2.qti.av1.decoder on the Adreno 740
# dropped 521 of 1200 frames of NR14_00 (22-23 fps), dav1d frame-parallel plays it and the opening at 30 fps with no drops (dm/games/README.md av1_decoder)
av1_decoder
# ---- Recommended settings (the launcher, Recommend.java; dm/games/README.md recommend) ----
# Phone's own driver Qualcomm's before 512.800 (driverID 8, VkPhysicalDeviceProperties.driverVersion major 512, minor below 800: the host's own qcom_old rule, vka_dev.c):
# an installed Turnip (driverID 18, MESA_TURNIP). README.md "Tested devices": on the AYN Thor (Adreno 740) the stock 512.676.53 runs with faults, characters and some
# foliage lit dark, dungeon at about 25 fps (GPU 36 ms); Turnip T30 and Gen8 V39 play the dungeon at 29-30 fps with characters correct; and README.md "Rendering
# fixes": "the stock driver stays not recommended for play"
recommend
# Every phone: FSR 3.1 as the Upscaler (the DLSS stand-in's DM_VK_DLSS=4). README.md "DLSS on a stand-in", per #151: finer detail than GSR 2 (c2) and about 30-40 % less
# unexplained flicker in camera pans and dashes, still edges equal at the default sharpness 0.5; the cost about 2 ms more GPU on Turnip, about 34 against 26 ms on an older
# stock driver (#151), about 3 ms more on the Pad 3's stock 512.800. It runs on Turnip and on Qualcomm's own driver, switches live, is clean with frame generation where GSR 2 is.
# A driver row sets only the driver, so this row and the one above apply independently; a player's own Upscaler choice is kept
recommend
# Android, resolution: the game builds six render configurations (output size, render size its DLSS takes to the output, shadow and level-of-detail settings; slots main+0x223e0b0)
# and picks one by the performance mode (Boost: the docked family, Normal: the handheld one), the graphics scale and the display's largest buffer, again on each notification 31.
# The host writes the player's output (DM_WINDOW_SIZE) and render size (DM_RENDER_PCT: 33 / 50 / 59 / 67 / 100 % of it) into all six and answers the performance mode from the graphics
# quality (DM_GFX_QUALITY: quality = Boost, the docked shadows and detail; performance = Normal, the handheld ones), and the largest buffer from the output (the game cuts an output
# larger than that buffer), at least 2 (2560x1440) under quality and 1 (1920x1080) under performance (hle_render.c). The game's own sizes, C0 to C5: 2560x1440 / 1280x720 docked
# scaled down to it while the game's own 1008 MiB render target pool is in use (rt_pool below sizes the pool for the setting; DM_RENDER_UNCAPPED=1 lifts the cap; DM_NVN_POOLS=1
# logs the pools' high-water marks). Outputs from 720p up (min)
render_cfg
render_quality
# Android: the render target pool the game makes at main+0x646f88 (movz w9, #0x3f00, lsl #16: 1008 MiB, CPU_NO_ACCESS | GPU_CACHED | COMPRESSIBLE; its allocator's range
# follows the size it records) is sized at load for the setting the game starts with (loader.c rt_pool_apply): the game's own 1008 MiB while the render size is at most 1280x720
# and the output below 1440 lines; 1536 MiB, and render sizes up to 1920x1080, for a 1440 output or a larger render size; 2048 MiB, and up to 2560x1440, for a render size above
# 1920x1080 (1440p or 1152p at 100 %). A device of more than 12 GB (the low-RAM keys below do not apply) gets 1536 MiB at least. The loader writes the word before the text is
# sealed, after checking the build and the word. Its pages stay lazy on Android (render targets have their own Vulkan memory). Pool high-water marks in light scenes: 1002.9 MiB
# of 1008 at 2560x1440 / 1706x960 quality, 71.7-73.6 % of 1536 at that setting with the larger pool; about 720 MiB at 1080p 100 %. A change in the in-game panel that needs a
# larger pool is clamped to this start's size until the next start. DM_RT_POOL_MB=<MiB> sets the size on any device (0: the game's own)
rt_pool
# The operation mode stays handheld whatever the setting: the game reads it only for its controller check and its sound mix
op_mode
# The default output when the player has chosen none: 1920x1080 (with the render scale's 50 % and performance: the game's own handheld configuration)
android_window
# ---- Variants (patches.py VARIANT_CUTS; Game settings > Aspect ratio) ----
# 43: native 4:3 (cameras and UI laid out for 4:3, shown at 4:3): main only
variant
modules
romfs_marker
zip_store
# ---- Memory ----
# The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (Donkey Kong Bananza's figure, not measured here). The NPDM declares 64 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on.
# 256 MB in front + alias region + 256 MB stack region + heap region: Splatoon Raiders' split as a starting point, to be measured
mem_reserve
mem_alias
mem_stack
app_pool
sys_resource
# Android, devices of 12 GB or less only (MemTotal up to 12 GiB, the AYN Thor's 11 GiB): memory pools of 256 MiB or more placed by parts, and the texture cache at most
# 1024 MiB on top of the limit it measures. On the Thor (Adreno 740, Turnip) the placed memory went from 887 to 553 MiB, and the cache held at 1024 MiB with 6 prunes at 30 fps
# (with DM_VK_PLACE_PART_MB=256 and DM_VK_IMG_LIMIT_MB=1024, the same values). DM_VK_LOW_RAM=0 turns both off, =1 applies them on any device
low_ram_place_part_mb
low_ram_img_cache_max_mb
# Android, the same devices: GetInfo TotalMemorySize reports 5632 MiB instead of app_pool's 9216; the pool, the map limit and SetHeapSize stay app_pool (hle_svc.c
# reported_total). The game's SDK sizes its cache of freed pages from the total it reads at startup: on the Thor, after the long title sequence and a Continue into a battle,
# the alias region held about 4.65 GB against 5.54-6.26 GB at 9216, at 30 fps, and the game was stopped by the low-memory killer in 0 of 4 runs against 3 of 3 at 9216.
# A run that reported 4096 MiB mapped up to 4.28 GB past it with no failure
low_ram_app_pool_mb
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py) ----
shader_groups
shader_note
